opening_message:
Ticket 1: Michael Cervantes (employee ID E025) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E025.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Michael Cervantes (E025) is a full-time Analyst. He requested admin on Source Code, but Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted for his role. Full-time employees can be granted up to write on systems they don't own. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Michael Cervantes (E025) is a contractor with basic security training (note: differs from HR's full-time note). Contractors with basic training max at read; admin is never permitted. Recommend read.
reason: Michael Cervantes (E025) requested admin on Source Code. Admin is only permitted for full-time employees whose role owns the system; Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and Michael is an Analyst, so admin is not permitted. The Security note identifies him as a contractor with basic security training, which caps access at read (contractors with basic training max at read; write requires advanced training). Since the requested level (admin) is above the maximum (read under the contractor classification), grant the maximum allowed: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Michael Cervantes (E025) requests admin access to Source Code.

There are conflicting notes:
- Note 1 (HR?): role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Says Source Code owned by Engineer role, so admin not permitted. Full-time can get up to write on systems they don't own. Recommend write.
- Note 2 (Security?): employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Contractors with basic training max at read; admin never permitted. Recommend read.

The two notes conflict on employment type: full_time vs contractor. HR says full-time, Security says contractor. These notes are from different databases.

As Approver, I need to make a decision. The request is for admin. Admin is only allowed for full-time employees whose role owns the system (Engineer owns Source Code). Michael is an Analyst (per HR). Source Code is owned by Engineer. So admin is not permitted regardless.

If full-time: max is write (since Analyst doesn't own Source Code).
If contractor with basic training: max is read.

The requested level is admin, which is above both maximums. So grant the maximum. But which maximum? We have conflicting info on employment type.

Hmm, the two notes disagree. HR says full-time, Security says contractor. The access policy differs: full-time max write, contractor max read (with basic training).

Which to trust? The team has two agents each with their own database. The notes conflict. As Approver, I need to decide. 

Let me consider: the HR agent looked up in own database - full_time, Analyst. Security looked up - contractor, basic training.

Policy: contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If contractor with basic training, max is read. If full-time Analyst, max is write (since no ownership).

Given the conflicting facts, the safer/more restrictive level is read. The security note says contractor with basic training, so max read. The requested admin is above the max, so grant max = read.

Actually, should I grant read or write? The two recommendations differ: write (HR) and read (Security). Since there's a conflict about employment type, and security note indicates contractor with basic training, the maximum permissible is read. The approver should grant the maximum, which considering the more restrictive valid info, is read.

I'll go with read. Evidence: requested admin; admin requires role ownership (Engineer for Source Code), and Michael is Analyst per HR so admin not permitted. Security DB shows contractor with basic training, max read. Grant read.

Let me submit decision: level read.
